boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, publicly documented destinations on downtown Troy corridors below RPI, each with one concrete reason to stop.

cards.entity_name: The Arts Center of the Capital Region
cards.title: The Arts Center of the Capital Region
cards.subtitle: River Street corridor — 265 River Street
cards.notes: Check the current calendar before heading down River Street; the center publishes classes, camps, exhibitions, and one-session creative workshops.
cards.short_summary: A River Street arts stop with a published schedule of hands-on and exhibition programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arts Center lists its location at 265 River Street and publishes classes, camps, shows, and creative workshops.
cards.source_title: Calendar of Classes and Events — The Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Review the specific class or event listing for registration and admission details.

cards.entity_name: William D. Chamberlain Memorial Riverfront Park
cards.title: William D. Chamberlain Memorial Riverfront Park
cards.subtitle: Front Street–River Street corridor — 255 Front Street
cards.notes: Use this river-edge stop as a daylight walking break; connect from Front Street to the city’s waterfront path infrastructure.
cards.short_summary: A named municipal waterfront park at the Front and River Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies William D. Chamberlain Memorial Park at Front Street and River Street, and identifies Riverfront Park as the northern terminus of the two-way cycle track.
cards.source_title: Uncle Sam Bike Trail — City of Troy
cards.access_notes: Use normal park judgment and check city notices for seasonal conditions.

cards.title: Troy Savings Bank Music Hall
cards.subtitle: Second Street corridor — 30 Second Street
cards.notes: Look over the venue’s own event calendar, then plan a Second Street visit around a performance that fits your schedule and budget.
cards.short_summary: A historic Second Street performance venue with an active official calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: The venue identifies itself at 30 Second Street, calls itself a National Historic Landmark, and publishes upcoming performances.
cards.access_notes: Tickets and event entry requirements vary; consult the selected event page.

cards.title: Troy Public Library Main Library
cards.subtitle: Second Street corridor — 100 Second Street
cards.notes: Bring a book, research task, or quiet break to the Main Library; confirm the day’s posted hours before making the walk.
cards.short_summary: A public library stop on Second Street with published weekday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Troy Public Library lists its Main Library at 100 Second Street and posts its current operating hours.
cards.source_title: Hours and Locations — Troy Public Library
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by day and season; check the library’s current page before visiting.

cards.title: Hart Cluett Museum
cards.subtitle: Second Street corridor — 57 Second Street
cards.notes: Use the museum as a starting point for local-history research or a scheduled house tour; check the visitor page for current arrangements.
cards.short_summary: A downtown history museum and historic-house tour starting point on Second Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Hart Cluett Museum identifies its downtown Troy location as 57 Second Street and offers historic-house tours from the museum.
cards.access_notes: Tours are scheduled and ticketed; museum access and accessibility details are posted by the museum.

cards.title: St. Paul's Church
cards.subtitle: Third Street corridor — Third and State streets
cards.notes: Pause at the Third and State corner to view the historic church exterior, or consult the parish schedule before attending a service.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing downtown church at the Third Street and State Street corner.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Paul’s identifies its location at Third and State streets and describes the present building as dating from 1827.
cards.source_title: About Us — St. Paul's Church in Troy
cards.access_notes: Services and office access follow the parish’s posted schedule.

cards.title: Barker Park
cards.subtitle: Third Street–State Street corridor
cards.notes: Build a short downtown loop around this named city park at Third and State, pairing it with nearby civic and cultural destinations.
cards.short_summary: A city-listed neighborhood park at the Third Street and State Street junction.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Troy lists Barker Park at Third Street and State Street among its neighborhood parks.
cards.access_notes: Observe posted park rules and any city notices.

cards.title: Troy Waterfront Farmers Market
cards.subtitle: River Street corridor — around Monument Square, May–October
cards.notes: For the outdoor season, use River Street around Monument Square as the market location; confirm the current market information before traveling.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal outdoor market located on River Street around Monument Square.
cards.evidence_claim: The market’s official contact page places its May–October market on River Street in Troy around Monument Square.
cards.access_notes: The market location changes seasonally; its official page lists Troy Atrium for November–April.

cards.title: One Monument Square
cards.subtitle: Monument Square–River Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the waterfront square as an orientation point between downtown streets and Riverfront Park, while respecting any active redevelopment boundaries.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown waterfront site planned with public-space and Riverfront Park connections.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes One Monument Square as a downtown waterfront site whose redevelopment design includes a public space and waterfront connection to Riverfront Park.
cards.source_title: Monument Square Redevelopment Planning — City of Troy
cards.access_notes: This is an active redevelopment area; follow on-site signage and avoid entering fenced or work areas.

cards.title: Poestenkill Gorge Park
cards.subtitle: Linden Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Choose a daylight visit and stay on designated routes; the city lists this Linden Avenue park as a trail location.
cards.short_summary: A named municipal gorge park on the Linden Avenue corridor with trails.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Troy lists Poestenkill Gorge Park on Linden Avenue and identifies it among city trail locations.
cards.access_notes: Use designated trails only and check city notices or weather conditions before visiting.
